Week in brief

Entra CBA documentation records tolerance for missing CRL endpoints; most other movement is guidance

The week of 26 May was overwhelmingly a Microsoft Learn maintenance cycle: 2,430 changes included 2,419 updates, 10 new pages, one removal, and no Message Center entries. The clearest substantive item is a documented certificate-based authentication behavior change. Other notable exceptions are new Copilot investigation guidance, security-control checks, Source of Authority migration planning, and an access-package/PIM behavior reference. Many remaining entries are routine integration, configuration, and troubleshooting refreshes rather than evidence of a broad service release.

  • Entra ID · Authentication
    Certificate-based authentication now documents support for issuers without CRL endpoints

    Changed behavior: the Microsoft Entra ID What's New material states that a certificate authority can be uploaded without a CRL endpoint and that certificate-based authentication will not fail when an issuing CA has no CRL specified. The CBA technical deep dive and federation/configuration articles were also refreshed. No GA or preview designation is supplied. Administrators troubleshooting CBA should revisit their CA/CRL assumptions against the updated guidance; the evidence does not say that existing tenants must1

  • Security Copilot · Fundamentals
    Copilot guidance expands across recommendations and ID Governance investigations

    New pages cover Microsoft Entra Recommendations with Microsoft Security Copilot, entitlement-management insights, and Access Reviews; an updated page also addresses investigating Entra recommendations. The summaries describe using Entra skills or Copilot to assess tenant health, investigate identity incidents, and analyze access-review data. These are documentation additions, not proof of a new rollout: availability, licensing, and automatic enablement are not stated.

  • Entra ID · Governance
    New security guidance targets application URI hygiene and privileged access controls

    New Microsoft Entra ID pages address dangling or abandoned domain redirect URIs, standing Global Administrator access to Azure subscriptions, access controls for governance Logic Apps, and monitoring and alerting for privileged-role activations. The existing guidance on restrictions for application identifier URIs was also updated. This is security guidance and review material, not evidence of new enforcement, changed defaults, or a remediation deadline.

  • Entra ID · Fundamentals
    Source of Authority migration receives a new planning guide

    A new Microsoft Entra ID article covers migrating Source of Authority from Active Directory to Microsoft Entra ID, including prerequisites, supported scenarios, and step-by-step guidance for architects and administrators. The evidence supports a new planning resource, not a newly announced GA capability, required transition, or automatic tenant change. Hybrid identity teams considering the move should use the supported-scenario and prerequisite information in their planning.

  • ID Governance · Governance
    Access-package and PIM timing behavior is clarified

    ID Governance added and then updated a reference for groups managed by Privileged Identity Management with access packages, specifically cases where access-package assignment periods and PIM policy periods do not align. The entry is a behavior reference rather than evidence of a new PIM or entitlement-management feature. The supplied summary does not state which period prevails, so governance teams should consult the full reference before changing time-bound access designs.

For Entra administrators

Review certificate-based authentication assumptions first, then route the new security, governance, SOA, and Copilot material to the relevant owners. The supplied evidence does not establish GA or preview status, licensing, enforcement changes, mandatory deadlines, or a forced migration for these items. The single removed item is not identified, so no retirement action can be inferred.

This period briefing was generated by AI from the tracked Microsoft Learn and Message Center changes.

When configured, Microsoft Entra ID automatically provisions and de-provisions users and groups to Adobe Identity Management (SAML) using the Microsoft Entra provisioning service. Howto Configure Recommendation Email Notifications

Updated

The email notifications provide a basic summary of the specific recommendation with a link to the related area of the Microsoft Entra admin center. The email also includes a link to related documentation so you can learn more about the recommendation and how to resolve it. These emails are enabled by default, aren't promotional or marketing emails, and don't contain any upselling content. These emails are purely informational and designed to help you act quickly when a new recommendation is available.

Updated

An ongoing challenge for helpdesk is verifying the identity of callers seeking help, especially in remote interactions via phone, chat, or email. Traditional methods such as personally identifiable information (PII) and knowledge-based authentication are no match for today’s sophisticated attackers, who leverage phishing, social engineering, and even AI-powered voice cloning to bypass defences. The consequences are serious: under pressure, helpdesk agents may unintentionally expose sensitive data or authorize fraudulent actions.
